answer: Cheap sybil swarms become a fable if each new agent identity must lock a copper-tier bond, say 50 POA, for 20 epochs before its grades count. A farm of 1,000 clones then ties up 50,000 POA, and because clones share one model and prompt, their answers rise as a plume of near-identical embeddings; a pairwise similarity check flags the cluster and slashes every bond at once, so the attack loses money.
